# Streaming GPU-based Voxel Carving

Also called: Accelerated volumetric reconstruction from uncalibrated camera views

## Overview
A streaming GPU-based voxel carving method that creates an explicit volume, avoids 3D texture drawbacks by using only surface voxels in a GPU-optimal 2D data representation, and minimizes GPU-CPU data transfer through effective load balancing [S1, unofficial]. It differs from its parent method, Voxel Carving, by explicitly optimizing for graphics hardware trends to maintain interactivity, and from previous approaches like [LiMS04], [WoeKoch04], and [ZacKar04] by avoiding the continuous access and dual-texture overhead inherent in 3D texture-based representations [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
The method tackles computational costs of voxel carving by leveraging the massive parallelism of modern graphics hardware. It constructs an explicit volume representation that can be modified interactively. The core innovation lies in the data structure and processing pipeline: instead of storing the entire volumetric grid in 3D textures, it employs a GPU-optimal two-dimensional data representation containing only surface voxels. This approach minimizes the memory footprint and bandwidth requirements. Furthermore, the method implements a form of effective load balancing to minimize the cost of inter-processor communication between the CPU and GPU, combining the optimal features of both processors [S1, unofficial].

Specific algorithmic steps, data layouts, and formulas are Not given in the sources. The sources describe the architectural choices (explicit volume, 2D surface-only representation, load balancing) but do not provide the implementation details required to code the method from scratch.

## Subtopics

### [Parallel Voxel Carving on GPU](14001-parallel-voxel-carving-on-gpu.md)
A variant that explicitly defines the thread-to-voxel mapping strategy (y-axis columns) and the specific data layout (8-byte quantized planes) required for high-throughput parallel execution, building on the streaming and load-balancing principles of this method.

## Operating characteristics
The method is designed for interactive performance. The authors report interactive framerates for a scene voxel resolution of $256 \times 256 \times 128$ [S1, unofficial]. It avoids the drawbacks of continuous access patterns and the need to use two 3D textures simultaneously, which were limitations of prior 3D texture-based approaches [S1, unofficial]. By minimizing GPU-CPU data transfer, it reduces the bottleneck associated with inter-processor communication [S1, unofficial].

## Background
This method was developed to address the computational costs of voxel carving in the context of latest graphics hardware trends at the time of publication [S1, unofficial]. It contrasts with previous approaches such as LiMS04, WoeKoch04, and ZacKar04, which either sacrificed interactivity for speed or relied on 3D texture representations with inherent drawbacks [S1, unofficial].
